value.text:
q03.

**`postgres.DB` — `store/db/postgres/postgres.go`**

The PostgreSQL implementation of the `store.Driver` interface is the struct named `DB` in package `postgres`:

```16:40:store/db/postgres/postgres.go
type DB struct {
	db      *sql.DB
	profile *profile.Profile
}

func NewDB(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
	...
	db, err := sql.Open("postgres", profile.DSN)
	...
	var driver store.Driver = &DB{
		db:      db,
		profile: profile,
	}
	return driver, nil
}
```

A few supporting details:

- The struct is constructed via `postgres.NewDB`, which opens a connection using the `github.com/lib/pq` driver (blank-imported at the top of the same file) and returns it as a `store.Driver`.
- It's wired up in the driver factory at `store/db/db.go`, where `profile.Driver == "postgres"` dispatches to `postgres.NewDB`. The sibling implementations follow the same pattern in `store/db/sqlite` and `store/db/mysql`, so each package has its own struct also named `DB`.
- The remaining methods of the `store.Driver` interface for PostgreSQL are spread across the other files in `store/db/postgres/` (for example `memo.go`, `user.go`, and `attachment.go`), all defined as methods on this same `*DB` receiver.
